title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Labour change and budget reduction
sections.summary: A motion to reduce Head S Estimates by $100 is moved amid profound labour change, ageing demographics and a historically low fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head S of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Singapore is going through a period of profound labour change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We are seeing the effects of an ageing demographic and our total fertility rate is at a historical low.

sections.label: First Industry Transformation Maps
sections.summary: The first Industry Transformation Maps were introduced in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Our first Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) were introduced in 2016.

sections.label: Platform Workers Trilateral Group
sections.summary: The Platform Workers Trilateral Group showed in 2025 how collaboration can address complex challenges such as illegal platform work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The Platform Workers Trilateral Group demonstrated in 2025 how effective collaboration can address complex challenges, such as illegal platform work.

sections.label: Three Budget priorities
sections.summary: Three Budget priorities are put forward for this new phase of labour transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In this new phase of labour transformation, I would like to put forward three Budget priorities.

sections.label: Foreign manpower and productivity
sections.summary: Foreign manpower must be calibrated with industry upgrading, productivity gains must raise wages, and eight occupations are to be added to the NTS-OL in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Foreign manpower must be calibrated alongside deeper industry upgrading so that productivity, not labour cost suppression, drives competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Third, productivity gains must translate into real wage uplift, especially for lower-wage and at-risk workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Job redesign and AI adoption must be linked directly to wage progression, so transformation narrows inequality rather than widens it because ultimately, every worker matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Their deployment must drive productivity and translate into better jobs and stronger wage outcomes for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: I note the Ministry's intention to add eight occupations from the social services, food services and transportation sectors to the Non-traditional Sources Occupation List (NTS-OL) in 2026.

sections.label: Conditions for NTS-OL firms
sections.summary: Firms accessing NTS-OL manpower should commit to structured local training, skills transfer from foreign workers and job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Firms that access NTS-OL manpower should also commit to structured training for locals, skills transfer from foreign workers and job redesign that improves work processes.

sections.label: Act protections extended to workers
sections.summary: An amendment extended the Act's protections to 430,000 more workers, comprising managers and executives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of its more far-reaching amendments was to extend the Act's protections to 430,000 more workers, comprising managers and executives.

sections.label: Larger companies retrenchment pay
sections.summary: Larger companies with more than 25 workers should be expected to pay at minimum one month for every year of service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Larger companies, those with more than 25 workers, should be expected to pay more at minimum, one month for every year of service, which is the norm for unionised companies.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits review question
sections.summary: MOM is asked to confirm if retrenchment benefits are under discussion in the current review under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can MOM confirm if retrenchment benefits are a subject under discussion as part of the current review under the Act?

sections.label: Industrial Relations Act executive representation clarity
sections.summary: MOM is asked to clarify section 17(3) exclusions, by amending guidelines or the Industrial Relations Act, so union representation of executives is clearer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: By the same token, the Industrial Relations Act was last amended more than a decade ago, in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the years that followed, unions which have sought to extend their scope of representation to include executives and have met with some difficulties because the exclusions set out in section 17(3) are too broadly worded, thereby giving employers the opportunity to claim that even low- and mid-level executive employees fall within them, whereas the intent behind the law was only to exclude those who are at senior management levels and carry out functions which genuinely give rise to a conflict of interest if they are represented by a union.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can I request MOM to look into providing greater clarity through a firmer and clearer articulation on this point, either through amending the guidelines or amending the Industrial Relations Act for statutory clarity?

sections.label: Jobseeker Support cap and early notice
sections.summary: MOM is urged to raise the Jobseeker Support cap from $5,000 to $7,600 and to give notice prior to retrenchment for early support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, we see more PMEs affected by involuntary unemployment than before and further exacerbated by the advent of GenAI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I strongly urge MOM to consider expanding the Jobseeker Support scheme cap from the current $5,000 to $7,600, which is the median salary of professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs), and I am speaking of PMETs and not even PMEs, which is much higher, so that the scheme remains meaningful, adequate and reflective of present‑day labour market realities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: By then, options are limited and intervention is reactive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I propose that the notice be done prior to retrenchment, so that early support can be activated, such as career coaching, job matching, redeployment and where possible, alternatives to retrenchment itself.

sections.label: National apprenticeship systems and WSQ
sections.summary: Countries including Australia, France, Germany, India, Switzerland and Turkey have national-level apprenticeship systems, and the WSQ framework includes an assessment only pathway.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, countries as diverse as Australia, France, Germany, India, Switzerland and Turkey, have national-level apprenticeship systems.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) framework under the rubric of SkillsFuture includes an assessment only pathway.

sections.label: GRIT traineeship programme positions
sections.summary: WSG launched the GRIT programme for ITE, polytechnic and university graduates, but a search shows fewer than 100 open positions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Most recently, WSG launched the GRaduate in Industry Traineeship (GRIT) programme for graduates of ITE, polytechnics and universities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is a major step and one that I wholeheartedly support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But a quick search reveals less than 100 open positions.

sections.label: National OJT system proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Government subsidise the labour market gap and institutionalise a national OJT system for apprenticeships, internships and mentorships.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is precisely where the Government can step in by subsidising the gap that the labour market would otherwise leave unfulfilled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I propose that we institutionalise a national OJT system for apprenticeships, internships and mentorships.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit for internships
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Government will advocate for Singaporeans in underserved sectors, proposes SkillsFuture Credit for paid internships, and notes such programmes typically last six months to a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In other words, will the Government be an advocate for Singaporeans that have ambitions to contribute to traditionally underserved sectors of the economy that nevertheless are passed to meaningful middle-class secure jobs?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, to encourage buy in from the corporate side.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I further propose that workers be allowed to apply their SkillsFuture Credit toward paid internship programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, in line with standard practice, such apprenticeships and internships can typically be short term, six months to a year —

sections.label: Lower-wage income growth reversal
sections.summary: Lower-wage workers' income growth once outpaced the median, but from 2024 to 2025 median real income growth exceeded theirs, which the speaker calls a warning signal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Lower-wage workers saw income growth that outpaced the median.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, from 2024 to 2025, median real income growth exceeded that of lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: This reversal, though modest, is a warning signal.

sections.label: Productivity in PWM sectors
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers reaffirmed productivity as the foundation for sustainable wage growth, and the speaker asks MOM about measurable sectoral productivity gains in PWM sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers reaffirmed productivity as the foundation for sustainable wage growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore ask MOM, have we seen measurable sectoral productivity gains in PWM sectors?

sections.label: Workfare threshold and underemployment monitoring
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising the Workfare Income Supplement income threshold to $3,500 and urges closer monitoring of non-time-based involuntary underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: After all, while real incomes for the lowest percentile showed significant progress in 2024, this comes on the heel of many years of falling behind median real income growth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I believe that it is time to disproportionately raise the income threshold for the Workfare Income Supplement to $3,500, to better support those who are working hard to make ends meet but struggling under the burden of high costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I am particularly concerned about non-time-based involuntary underemployment in Singapore and urge for closer monitoring of this trend.

sections.label: Youth resident unemployment rate
sections.summary: The unemployment rate for residents below 30 was 5.5% in September 2025, almost twice the national resident unemployment rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The unemployment rate for residents below 30 was 5.5% in September 2025, almost twice the national resident unemployment rate.

sections.label: Proposed Youth Wage Credit Scheme
sections.summary: A proposed Youth Wage Credit Scheme would give micro and small enterprises a 20% wage credit over the first three months of graduates' first permanent positions, capped at $1,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To support young Singaporeans in facilitating a smoother entry into the workforce, I propose a Youth Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This initiative incentivises micro and small enterprises to offer the Institute of Technical Education (ITE), Lasalle College of the Arts, the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, polytechnic and university graduates their first permanent positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will provide a 20% wage credit over the first three months of employment, covering the critical probation and initial training period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government could co-fund 20% of their salary with the payout capped at $1,000 per month.

sections.label: Wage credit versus GRIT places
sections.summary: GRIT is limited to 800 places, while the wage credit could support a much larger proportion of the 53,000 or so students graduating each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Crucially, while GRIT is limited to just 800 places, this wage credit could support a much larger proportion of the 53,000 or so students graduating each year.

sections.label: Declared interest and job mismatch
sections.summary: The speaker declares interest as a senior executive of an educational institute and worries about the mismatch between plentiful jobs and local workers willing to take them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I declare my interest as a senior executive of an educational institute that offers workplace learning and job redesign consultancy services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho
sentences.text: I worry about the mismatch between jobs that are plentiful in Singapore and the number of local workers who are willing to take them up.

sections.label: Redesigning jobs at scale
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether jobs such as nursing, security and skilled trades can be redesigned at scale so AI and robotics take over tedious aspects of work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho
sentences.text: My question is whether we can be bolder in redesigning jobs, such as nursing, security and skilled trades, at scale so that they become occupations our young people aspire to pursue, so that AI and robotics take over the tedious aspects of work, while workers contribute to service design, innovation and customer engagement.

sections.label: Career and skills passport access
sections.summary: The career and skills passport launched in November 2024, and more than 700,000 individuals accessed it as of November last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Tools like the career and skills passport launched in November 2024 reflect that ambition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We know that more than 700,000 individuals have accessed the passport as of November last year.

sections.label: Skills-first hiring survey findings
sections.summary: OECD and IAL index ranked Singapore 12 of 30, and an IHRP survey found 63% of hiring managers unfamiliar with skills-first hiring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The 2025 Skills-First Readiness and Adoption Index developed by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the Institute for Adult Learning ranked Singapore 12 out of 30 participating countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Relatedly, in a survey conducted by the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP), nine in 10 respondents were confident that skills-first hiring widens their organisation's talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, 63% of hiring managers, the people conducting interviews and on the front lines of recruitment, said they are unfamiliar with skills-first hiring practices.

sections.label: Qualifying salary and LQS increases
sections.summary: EP qualifying salary rises from $4,500 to $6,000, S Pass from $2,500 to $3,600 in 2027, and LQS to $1,800 in July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since 2020, the Employment Pass (EP) qualifying salary will rise from $4,500 to $6,000 next year, roughly a one-third increase in just over six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Over the same period, the S Pass qualifying salary has moved from $2,500 to $3,600 in 2027, about a 44% uplift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The LQS will increase to $1,800 in July.

sections.label: Assessing salary adjustments and competitiveness
sections.summary: It asks how MOM assesses whether qualifying salary and LQS adjustments strengthen the Singaporean core without eroding competitiveness, and whether a framework exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How does MOM assess whether cumulative qualifying salary and LQS adjustments are strengthening the Singaporean core without eroding competitiveness?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there a structured framework to assess sectoral sensitivity, particularly in industries with thin margins or limited automation pathways?

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Senior Employment Credit was extended again this year, after extensions in 2023 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, to the Senior Employment Credit, extended again this year after extensions in 2023 and 2025.

sections.label: PWCS minimum wage and traineeship integration
sections.summary: It proposes retaining the PWCS minimum wage increase at $100 instead of $200, and integrating traineeship and place-and-train programmes with time-limited salary support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In addition, the minimum wage increase to qualify for PWCS support should be retained at $100 instead of the Government's change to set it at $200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Third, integrate the Government's traineeship and place-and-train programmes, such that employers get time-limited salary support to hire any jobseeker who has been actively looking for a job for six months.

sections.label: Advisory support for SME job redesign
sections.summary: It asks whether MOM can ensure the package is streamlined with clear advisory support for SMEs conducting structured job redesign and skills mapping.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can MOM ensure the package is streamlined with clear advisory support to help SMEs conduct structured job redesign and skills mapping exercises?

sections.label: AI productivity and wage measurement
sections.summary: Asking how MOM will measure whether enterprises redesign jobs alongside technology adoption if AI raises productivity but wages stay flat.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If AI raises productivity, but wages remain flat, then confidence will certainly erode.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, my question to the Minister is this: how will MOM measure whether enterprises are redesigning jobs alongside technology adoption?

sections.label: Career health screening for PMEs
sections.summary: Proposes adding a nationally standardised, subsidised career health screening for PMEs aged 35 to 65 to MyCareersFuture and the NTUC AI career coach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, with PMEs forming 64.2% of our resident workforce and Singapore becoming a super-aged society, strengthening the career health of PMEs in their 40s, 50s and early 60s is increasingly urgent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture participation reached more than 600,000 in 2025, job redesign and upskilling efforts continue through the Company Training Committees (CTCs) and the Alliance for Action (AfA) on Multi-stage Careers adds further scaffolding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But to sustain employability, we must now make career health mainstream, preventive and easy to act on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I propose augmenting MyCareersFuture and the NTUC AI career coach with a nationally standardised, subsidised career health screening for PMEs aged 35 to 65.

sections.label: Co-funded renewal scheme for job redesign
sections.summary: A co-funded renewal scheme could support job redesign, redeployment into growth areas and employer validated training, as retirement and re-employment ages rise to 64 and 69.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: A co-funded renewal scheme could support job redesign, redeployment into growth areas and role specific, employer validated training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This is essential, as retirement and re-employment ages will rise to 64 and 69 this year.

sections.label: Structured career pathways for skilled tradesmen
sections.summary: Welcomes Government working with employers, Labour Movement, trade associations and institutes of higher learning to develop structured career pathways for skilled tradesmen.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Chairman, I welcome the direction that the Government will work with employers, the Labour Movement, trade associations and institutes of higher learning to develop structured career pathways for skilled tradesmen, so that this inclination towards hands-on and "heart" jobs can see how they can advance and how they can build a career.

sections.label: Rewarding skills and employer standards
sections.summary: Urges employers to support and fairly remunerate trade workers and Government to work with industry on training, mentorship and assessment standards, especially in SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Skills take time to build, deep mastery should be rewarded through structured progression, skills-based pay bands and credible steps from apprentice to specialist to titles, such as master craftsman.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Third, firms must be part of the solution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I urge employers to support and fairly remunerate trade workers, and for the Government to work with the industry to build consistent standards for training, mentorship and assessment, especially in SMEs where the capability varies.

sections.label: Manpower projections for critical skilled trades
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry tracks medium- to long-term manpower projections for critical skilled trades supporting digital infrastructure and the green transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry track medium- to long-term manpower projections for critical skilled trades, especially those supporting digital infrastructure and the green transition?

sections.label: National Master Trades Accreditation framework
sections.summary: The Government is asked to consider developing a national tiered certification recognising advanced trade mastery and creating career transition avenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider developing a National Master Trades Accreditation framework – a national tiered certification that recognises advanced trade mastery, similar to chartered professionals in other sectors and create a new avenue for career switchers and career transition for segments of our workforce?

sections.label: PWM and income inequality
sections.summary: The PWM led lower-wage workers to the strongest percentage growth in real incomes, and income inequality is at its lowest recorded level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Thanks to the PWM, our lower-wage workers experienced the strongest percentage growth in their real incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Income inequality today is at its lowest level on record.

sections.label: Merging SSG and WSG
sections.summary: The move to merge SSG and WSG is described as a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The move to merge SSG and WSG is thus a step in the right direction.

sections.label: Caregivers considering leaving jobs
sections.summary: In NTUC's recent Economic Sentiments survey, close to one in two caregivers surveyed considered leaving their job due to caregiving stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: In NTUC's recent survey of Economic Sentiments, close to one in two caregivers surveyed considered leaving their job due to stress from caregiving.

sections.label: CPF top-up for caregivers
sections.summary: A one-off means-tested CPF top-up supports retirement adequacy of Singaporeans aged 50 and above, but concern is raised for about 13,000 out-of-workforce elderly caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The one-off means-tested Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-up to provide additional support to boost retirement adequacy of Singaporeans aged 50 and above is a step in the right direction, especially for our caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: However, there is one group that I am particularly concerned about – the 13,000 or so who are out of the workforce to care for their elderly.

sections.label: CPF top-ups and senior employment
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to study targeted CPF top-ups for middle- to lower-income caregivers and to track whether senior employment rates are affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We ask the Ministry to study providing targeted CPF top-ups for middle- to lower-income caregivers who have left employment for caregiving and who lack retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: These measures would help provide greater support and earlier assurance for our workers that their sacrifices made for caregiving will not unduly compromise their own long-term needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to ask the Ministry on its plans to study and consider measures to better support our caregivers' employability and retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTUC and the unions have constantly advocated for the reinstatement of CPF contribution rates for mature workers to match those of younger workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We thank the Government for continuing with the increases and for also extending the CPF Transition Offset to support employers implementing the increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, as Singapore's workforce ages amidst a challenging and hyper-competitive environment, how does the Ministry track outcomes and ensure senior employment rates are not affected, especially for those aged 55 to 64?

sections.label: CPF Special Account closure uncertainty
sections.summary: After the CPF Special Account closed in 2025, some members were uncertain about growing their monies for their golden years, especially after 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Following the closure of the CPF Special Account in 2025, some members expressed uncertainty about growing their monies to prepare for their golden years, especially after turning 55.

sections.label: Global portfolio returns
sections.summary: A typical global portfolio of 65% equities and 35% bonds would have earned around 6% per year in Singapore dollar terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: Over that period a typical global investment portfolio of 65% equities and 35% bonds would have earned around 6% per year in Singapore dollar terms.

sections.label: Closing CPFIS Special Account
sections.summary: Given the Prime Minister's update that three in four CPFIS Special Account investors underperformed the 4% risk-free rate, the Ministry should consider closing the CPFIS scheme for the Special Account once the LRIS launches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: In fact, given the Prime Minister's update last week that three in four CPFIS investors using the Special Account underperformed the 4% risk-free rate, the Ministry should consider closing the CPFIS scheme for the Special Account once the LRIS is launched.

sections.label: Budget 2026 life-cycle scheme
sections.summary: Budget 2026 announced a low-cost life-cycle investment scheme providing a new option to manage one's CPF funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: In Budget 2026, the announced low-cost life-cycle investment scheme provides a new option to manage one's CPF funds.

sections.label: CPFIS investors underperforming since 2016
sections.summary: The majority of CPFIS investors have underperformed the CPF's risk-free interest rates since 2016, when the CPF Advisory Panel studied the issue and first proposed the LRIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: The trends are worrying because the majority of CPFIS investors have been underperforming the CPF's risk-free interest rates since 2016 when the CPF Advisory Panel that I sat on studied this issue and first proposed the LRIS.

sections.label: LRIS fees and success measures
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there will be an all-in fee cap, and how the Ministry will measure success when the scheme is implemented in 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Will there be an all-in fee cap, including management fees, platform costs and transaction expenses, so members see one transparent figure?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Lastly, in his round-up speech, the Prime Minister did mention that the roll-out of the life-cycle investment option is slated for 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: When the scheme is implemented in 2028, how will the Ministry measure success in terms of participation rates, risk-adjusted returns and improvements in retirement adequacy outcomes for CPF members?

sections.label: Tripartite Maritime Training Award
sections.summary: SMOU, MPA and MOM launched the enhanced Tripartite Maritime Training Award, which supports mid-career transitions into maritime with monthly stipends.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Last year, SMOU together with the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore, and MOM partner agencies, launched the enhanced Tripartite Maritime Training Award (TMTA).

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The TMTA supports the mid-career transitions into the maritime industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The trainees receive financial support in the form of a monthly stipend throughout their training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that the first batch of cadets under the enhanced scheme have all progressed to the sailing phase of their training and they will soon be joined by a larger second cohort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This is one example of the work being done to support displaced individuals and better align our workforce with the needs of the economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)

sentences.text: Can the Minister share what evidence exists on the inter-generational impact of caregiving?

sentences.text: Nearly half are in their prime working years, ages 40 to 59.

sentences.text: Employees with caregiving responsibilities should receive six days annually, three employer-paid and three Government-paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari
sentences.text: This has improved labour force participation of those in the ages of 55 to 64, from 69% in 2015 to 73% in 2025.

sections.label: Tripartite guidelines and TAFEP complaints
sections.summary: The tripartite guidelines give employees a right to request and a process for consideration but do not govern outcomes, and TAFEP received one complaint since December 2024 about the format of a rejection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan

sections.label: Flexible work legislation and presumptive right

sentences.text: Second, make flexible work a presumptive right for parents of children under three, where the nature of the job allows, not absolute or unconditional, just the starting position that an employer has to justify departing from, rather than a benefit that an employee must request.

sections.summary: The speaker supports the guidelines but asks MOM to recognise that not all employers, especially SMEs, have the capacity, manpower and HR expertise to implement formal FWA workflows effectively.

sentences.text: Chairman, I support the thrust of these guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: But I ask MOM to recognise a simple ground reality: not all employers, especially SMEs, have the capacity, manpower, HR expertise to implement this formal FWA workflows effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: If unaddressed, these guidelines risk becoming compliance issues rather than substance, particularly for SMEs.

sections.label: Salad shop owner work injury claim

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Chairman, sometime in mid-2025, a salad shop owner tragically passed away after an alleged fraudulent work injury claim that was filed against her.

sections.label: MOM support for SMEs
sections.summary: MOM could provide practical guidelines on workplace bullying, publish investigation protocols, help SMEs formulate inclusive employment schemes, and consolidate employer support schemes into a single platform, and the workplace fatal injury rate for 2025 fell to 0.96 per 100,000 workers from 1.2 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Third, MOM could maybe help employers, especially SMEs, to formulate inclusive employment schemes into day-to-day workable processes, so that support for persons with disabilities, women and caregivers can become operationally realistic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Fourth, MOM could consider consolidating employer support schemes and guidelines into a single, user-friendly platform, similar to what we have: SupportGoWhere, so SMEs can quickly understand what they qualify for and how to implement this support without heavy reliance on consultants or even middlemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: I am encouraged that the workplace fatal injury rate for 2025 has fallen to 0.96 per 100,000 workers, down from 1.2 in 2024.

sections.label: Mandating safety technologies
sections.summary: MOM should move towards mandating technologies like anti-collision systems, video analytics and fatigue detection in high-risk sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: In high-risk sectors, MOM should move towards mandating technologies such as anti-collision systems, video analytics to detect unsafe acts, and fatigue detection tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Public procurement policies should reward companies with strong WSH records and clear investments in risk elimination and job redesign.

sections.label: Working hours and fatigue safeguards

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: MOM should strengthen safeguards on working hours and rest periods, and require employers to implement formal fatigue risk management systems.

sections.label: Migrant worker recreation centres
sections.summary: The MOM, NTUC and Migrant Workers' Centre partnership runs recreational centres providing recreation, community activities and services to thousands weekly.

sentences.text: The partnership between MOM, NTUC and our Migrant Workers' Centre in managing recreational centres is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: These centres provide recreation, community activities and essential services such as groceries, remittance and telecommunications, serving thousands weekly.

sections.label: Employment and income growth
sections.summary: Singapore recorded 17 straight quarters of employment growth, 2.9% resident unemployment, and real income growth for median and lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As of December, last year, we have recorded 17 straight quarters of employment growth since we emerged from COVID-19 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our resident unemployment rate has remained low at 2.9%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Lower-wage workers saw real incomes grow by 15% from 2020 to 2025, or about 2.8% per annum, faster than the median worker.

sections.label: Graduate employment by December 2025

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: By December 2025, over eight in 10 university graduates from the 2025 cohort had already found employment and this is comparable to the 2024 cohort.

sections.label: Overseas Markets Immersion Programme expansion
sections.summary: WSG's Overseas Markets Immersion Programme, launched in 2024, will be expanded to help young professionals gain overseas exposure earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)

sections.label: Free AI tool subscriptions
sections.summary: Those taking selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive free subscriptions to premium versions of AI tools for six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As announced at Budget, those who take up selected SkillsFuture AI courses will receive free subscriptions to premium versions of best-in-class AI tools for six months.

sentences.text: Following the integration of Careers and Skills Passport with job portals, JobStreet and FastJobs, our partners found that job applications with verified credentials are 1.5 times more likely to be shortlisted by employers.

sentences.text: In total, our tools and initiatives have already helped over 800,000 individuals and 38,000 firms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The workgroup will release its recommendations in the second half of this year.

sentences.text: As previously announced, we will raise the retirement and the re-employment ages to 64 and 69 respectively on 1 July 2026, and this will keep us on track to raising them to 65 and 70 before 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In the interim, we will extend the Senior Employment Credit until December 2027 to continue supporting employers hiring senior workers.

sentences.text: As announced, we will increase CPF contribution rates in 2027 for senior workers by 1.5 percentage-points for workers aged above 55 to 60, and one percentage-point for workers aged above 60 to 65.

sections.label: CPF top-up for eligible Singaporeans
sections.summary: Eligible Singaporeans aged 50 and above with CPF balances below the prevailing Basic Retirement Sum will receive a CPF top-up of up to $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As announced, we will provide a CPF top-up of up to $1,500 for eligible Singaporeans aged 50 and above, with CPF balances below the prevailing Basic Retirement Sum.

sections.summary: The CPF Board will introduce a new investment scheme with life-cycle investment products that automatically shift to lower-risk assets via a glide-path as the investor grows older.

sentences.text: As the Prime Minister announced, the CPF Board will introduce a new investment scheme, with life-cycle investment products that will automatically shift to lower-risk assets via a glide-path, as the investor grows older.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will cap all-in fees to keep costs low and are prepared to provide some time-limited support to interested members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng

sections.label: ONE Pass holder numbers

sentences.text: Currently, over 8,000 individuals are on the ONE Pass, and many of them contribute to sectors which are critical to our future economy.

sentences.text: To strengthen our attractiveness to top talent in critical and emerging technologies like AI and quantum computing, we will introduce a new ONE Pass AI and Tech track in January 2027.

sections.label: EP minimum qualifying salary

sentences.text: As announced, we will raise the EP minimum qualifying salary from $5,600 to $6,000, in line with the wages of the top one-third of local PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Across all sectors, Work Permit numbers have grown by 186,000, or 27%.

sections.label: Levy framework rate reduction

sentences.text: Second, we will add eight new occupations to the Non-Traditional Source Occupation List (NTS-OL) from September 2026, in the areas of food services, social services and air transportation.

sentences.text: The redesigned SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit will also be launched late this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Companies can tap on the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit to further defray the out-of-pocket expenses of workforce transformation.

sections.label: Electrical trade uplift pilot

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will continue to support wage improvements for our lower-wage workers such as through raising the LQS.

sentences.text: We have extended it by two years to support businesses doing their part to uplift lower-wage workers.

sentences.text: Over 600 companies have tapped on the Company Training Committee Grant since August 2022.

sentences.text: Businesses have also expressed concerns over the potential leakage of confidential, market-sensitive information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are not ruling out any option, we are engaging, we review, this will be a comprehensive review, we are consulting tripartite partners on these issues and will update in due course.

sentences.text: So it balance, we are reviewing it, and I think Senior Minister of State Koh will provide further updates on the Employment Act review.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will make AI tools universally accessible, making it easier for Singaporeans to access AI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)

sections.label: Adapting workers, employers, government
sections.summary: Workers must stay adaptable, employers must invest in people, and Government will strengthen career and employment systems and keep protections fit for a changing workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Workers must stay adaptable, taking ownership of their skills and plan ahead for transitions over longer careers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Employers must continue to invest in their people, redesigning jobs, developing skills and creating workplaces where workers of all ages can contribute meaningfully.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Government will continue to walk alongside both, strengthening career and employment systems, uplifting HR capabilities, supporting transitions and keeping our employment protections fit for a changing workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This is how we turn longer working lives into a strength for Singapore, strengthening productivity, resilience and inclusion at the same time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: And our commitment to Singaporeans is this: as work changes, we will keep listening, keep assisting, and keep adapting, so that workers have the confidence to move forward and businesses have the support to grow through change.
